title: The Koszul locus of a map over a flat finitely presented base family is open and stable under base change (spaces)
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a commutative triangle X -> Y -> Z of spaces over S with both legs flat and locally of finite presentation, there is an open subspace U(f) subset X whose points are exactly where f is Koszul, and U(f') equals the inverse image of U(f) under any base change Z' -> Z. The retained proof is complete: openness of the Koszul locus follows from the lci definition's local-Koszul chart structure (definition-lci) plus the open-subspace existence lemma for spaces; the base-change statement is reduced through a four-stage surjective etale scheme presentation W' -> W x_Z Z' over V -> W x_Z Y over U -> V x_Y X (with V' = W' x_W V, U' = W' x_W U) to the cartesian diagram of scheme morphisms U' -> V' over U -> V, where the schemes-side twin (More on Morphisms, lemma base-change-lci-fibres) identifies the Koszul point sets T' = T x; etale maps are open on underlying spaces so the image description transfers, and |U'| -> |X'| surjectivity finishes. Retained author proof at lines 11400-11438.
